brief: Pricing page under seven simultaneous structural requirements
vision: The three tiers read as one set: same card edges, same inner padding, and the price sits in the same place on each.
The billing switch reads as a two-state control, and which state is active is visible without reading the labels.
The heading is one `<h1>` and reads as the page's title, not as a card's.
Inside a card the price is the largest element, and the period (/mo, /yr) is subordinate to it rather than the same size.
A contact-sales form with an email field is present, and it is reachable without competing with the plans for first attention.
code: Tiers render from `window.__DATA__` when it is an array, and the fallback is a real fallback rather than the same list under another name.
An annual price is shown, and it is computed from the monthly one rather than being a second hard-coded set that can drift. Showing no annual price does not satisfy this.
Plan names reach the DOM as text. Nothing from the data is interpolated into `innerHTML`.
The billing controls are real `<button>` elements and the email field is `<input type="email">` — the required semantics, not divs styled to look like them.
Every plan card contains a call-to-action link, and the page ends with a `<footer>`.
